method: electrocardiography (first post-stimulus inter-beat interval outside the 95% confidence interval of 10 pre-test intervals) plus a behavioural bioassay, with fresh sugarcane juice as the chemical stimulus and a 50 um micropipette tip as the touch stimulus

method: behavioural olfactory test: trained to sniff two boxes with absorbent paper strips, one with odorant (S+) and one with solvent (S-), opening the S+ box rewarded; start at a 100-fold liquid dilution and step down in 10-fold steps until discrimination failed, then an intermediate dilution
conditions: four female spider monkeys in two outdoor enclosures (6 x 4 x 4 m) at the Field Station Pipiapan; 30 trials (15 S+, 15 S-) per animal and condition; the paper tests 2-propylthietane, 2,2-dimethylthietane, 3-mercapto-3-methylbutan-1-ol, 3-mercapto-3-methylbutyl formate, 3-methyl-1-butanethiol and methyl-2-phenylethyl sulfide, with lowest dilutions all four animals discriminated from solvent between 1:3x10^6 and 1:3x10^8 (read from a page summary, not quoted); the 1 ppb figure is a ceiling for all six, not the value for each; the sentence before it points to Table 2 for per-odorant measures, which was not read; threshold is the most dilute stimulus all animals discriminated, so it is a group threshold; the same paper tests CD-1 mice and humans, not filed here; the odorants come from mustelids, small felids (cat, bobcat), skunk and red fox (Methods); the paper states that the spider monkey's only known mammalian predators, jaguar and cougar, have not been analysed for these odorants and that 'it seems unlikely that spider monkeys are regularly exposed to any of the six predator odorants tested here, at least in the context of predator avoidance'; with four of the six odorants (all but 2,2-dimethylthietane and 3-mercapto-3-methylbutan-1-ol) individual animals reached thresholds as low as 10 ppt; individual thresholds differed by factors of 10 to 1,000 depending on odorant, and sensitivity did not differ significantly between the six odorants
